title: Prepare the comparison arms and per-frame iteration record
description:
Make the single-frame, QC prototype and AFF3CT arms runnable in one comparison family on the current tree, with a per-frame iteration record. The earlier comparison reuses the first frames of the corpus while its quality statistics cover 128 frames, so equal iteration counts within the timed frames are unestablished.

## Background

The reuse paths are in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/investigation.md`, section Harness reuse. The arm and iteration semantics are fixed by the contract `arm-support` in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/plan.md`. The existing driver, runner journal and family tools stay; this work adds no timing framework, result schema or C++ counter. No timed measurement belongs to this work.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The arm catalogue resolves the QC prototype arm, and a distinct arm name built from a separate pinned tree, through the existing build records, confirmed by a non-timed smoke of the family tools.
- [hard] REQ-02: After timing, each gf2 and QC arm emits the iteration count of each worker and frame of the timed prefix, labelled direct. AFF3CT counts come from a post-timing replay on the counting prototype, labelled replay-derived, and a test shows replay decisions equal timed-worker decisions.
- [hard] REQ-03: The record is produced only after the timing loop ends, so the timed calls of the gf2 and AFF3CT arms are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: The QC arm's parity-check comparison with the corpus code covers the full relation, outside timing.
- [hard] REQ-05: The QC prototype's cap-zero path initializes its posterior from channel LLRs, with a test that a reused decoder exposes no stale posterior, and the prototype's contract tests pass on the current tree.

planning.outcome: Arms and per-frame iteration record ready for one comparison family

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One post-timing hook on existing arms, one catalogue registration, and a small prototype repair

title: Pilot the NR routes against AFF3CT and record the route decisions
description:
Run the current-tree pilot comparing the production single-frame route, the QC-aware intra-frame prototype and AFF3CT on NR BG1 Z=384, and record the QC and compact-lane decisions it informs. AFF3CT's matched flooding normalized min-sum decoder [Cassagne2019] leads gf2 on this code at one worker with one frame and at twelve workers with eight frames per worker, and the QC prototype's earlier timings are descriptive only.

## Background

Earlier results are in `dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/1358d6ab/outcome.md` and the candidate ranking in `dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/1362381c/aff3ct-gap-investigation.md`. The cells, campaign budget and decision rule are fixed by the contracts `nr-pilot-frame` and `qc-go-rule` in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/plan.md`. Timed runs execute only in the overnight benchmark window, and arming a window needs the owner's approval.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed pilot receipt on a recorded current-tree build covers the ten paired cells of `nr-pilot-frame`, with the iteration record of every arm and cell committed beside it.
- [hard] REQ-02: Before any timed run, QC posterior bits equal the canonical decoder's on the timed frames. A failure is recorded and stops the QC arm.
- [hard] REQ-03: A committed decision record applies `qc-go-rule` to the receipt, cites it, states the result that would have reversed the decision, and preserves the evidence under either outcome.
- [hard] REQ-04: The decision record decides the compact-lane and selective NR lane routing candidates after the receipt exists: it starts them with a named next falsifiable experiment in a new work item, or holds them with the reason.
- [hard] REQ-05: No production decoder behavior changes, and the gf2 and QC arms stay within `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md`. The record states AFF3CT's differences from that contract.

planning.outcome: NR pilot receipt with iterations, plus recorded QC and compact-lane decisions

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One family declaration on prepared arms; both decisions read its single receipt

title: Compare check-update variants and nominate at most one
description:
Compare two contract-preserving check-update variants with the production check update on DVB-T2 R1/2 and NR BG1 Z=384, and nominate at most one for confirmation. The check update is the only lead for DVB-T2, whose code has no QC partition, and it dominates the sampled one-frame profiles of both codes.

## Background

Production reaches `min_sum_check_row` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/min_sum.rs` on both losing single-frame routes. The variants, their isolation, cells and nomination rule are fixed by the contract `check-variants` in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/plan.md`; source findings are in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/investigation.md`, section Check-update path. Normalizing unsigned minima before signing, and a literal transplant of AFF3CT's min/max fold, both violate the numerical contract and are excluded. Timed runs execute only in the overnight benchmark window, and arming a window needs the owner's approval.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each variant's check-row output bits equal the independent scalar reference of `crates/gf2-coding/tests/ldpc_check_update_contract.rs`, including ties, signed zero, NaN, infinity and low degrees.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each variant's whole-decoder posterior bits equal an executable built from the unchanged production check update, on corpus frames and special-value frames, before any timed run. A mismatching variant is recorded and not timed.
- [hard] REQ-03: A committed pilot receipt on a recorded build compares each surviving variant with unchanged production at `w1-b1` and `p12-b8` on both codes.
- [hard] REQ-04: Committed disassembly of each measured variant's check row states whether the conditional branches of the reduction are removed.
- [hard] REQ-05: A committed record applies the nomination rule to the receipt and either names one variant with its patch or preserves the negative result. Production source stays unchanged.

planning.outcome: Two check-update variants compared on four cells, nominating at most one

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Both variants are bounded patches of one scalar function measured by existing family tools

title: Deliver the QC decoder core with its kernel and scalar fallback
description:
Implement QC-aware intra-frame decoding as a reusable library capability in `gf2-coding` over a safe kernel in `gf2-kernels-simd`, promoting the prototype. This work proceeds only on a recorded go decision for QC-aware intra-frame decoding, and a no-go closes it as obsolete without implementation.

## Background

`LdpcCode::from_quasi_cyclic` discards the QC description, so a library API must retain it. The prototype is `dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/f63a2464/survey/prototypes/src/qc.rs`. The obligations are fixed by the contract `qc-go-rule` in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/plan.md`; go-path findings are in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/investigation.md`, section Go path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A library API retains applicable QC structure for a code and reports its absence for a code that has none.
- [hard] REQ-02: Unsafe code lives only in `gf2-kernels-simd` with explicit safety contracts, a tested scalar fallback exists, and Rust 1.95 feasibility evidence covers any new intrinsic.
- [hard] REQ-03: Posterior bits equal the canonical decoder's for scalar and SIMD paths, including cap zero, decoder reuse, special values and both stopping modes.
- [hard] REQ-04: Decoder behavior stays within `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md`.

planning.outcome: Reusable QC decoder over a safe kernel with scalar fallback, matching canonical posteriors

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One decoder and one kernel family moved from an existing prototype

title: Route the QC decoder through canonical tuning and dispatch
description:
Make the QC decoder selectable through the canonical tuning and dispatch system over its declared domain, off the default route until confirmation passes. This work proceeds only on a recorded go decision for QC-aware intra-frame decoding, and a no-go closes it as obsolete without implementation.

## Background

Selection lives in `crates/gf2-coding/src/tuning.rs` and `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/route.rs`, which today express frame lanes versus single-frame. The domain and route rule are fixed by the contract `qc-go-rule` in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/plan.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `DecodeSelectors`, `CodingTuning` and `BatchRoute` express the frozen predicate of `qc-go-rule`, every exhaustive `BatchRoute` consumer handles the QC route, and every case outside the predicate keeps its existing route.
- [hard] REQ-02: The route passes `batch_soft_decoder_contract` and the LDPC batch contract suite, including forced fallback on hosts without the kernel.
- [hard] REQ-03: Tests show that the one-worker eight-frame case and every algorithm other than normalized min-sum keep their existing routes.
- [hard] REQ-04: The committed default envelope leaves the QC route unselected, and a candidate envelope selecting it exists for confirmation.
- [hard] REQ-05: The tuned comparison arm installs the candidate envelope, attaches QC structure only after an exact parity-check comparison with the corpus code outside timing, and reports the route each worker observed, so a measurement of the existing route cannot pass as QC.

planning.outcome: QC route selectable through canonical tuning with tested fallback

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One route variant added to the existing selector and route types

title: Confirm the integrated candidate and adopt it only if it qualifies
description:
Confirm any nominated check variant and any delivered QC route against pinned pre-change production under the frozen protocol, and adopt only what qualifies. Pilots are exploratory, so no production change is adopted on pilot evidence.

## Background

The family, stages, margins and adoption rule are fixed by the contract `adoption-family` in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/plan.md`. Timed runs execute only in the overnight benchmark window, and arming a window needs the owner's approval.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: With no nominated variant and no delivered route, a record states that production is unchanged and no campaign runs.
- [hard] REQ-02: Otherwise, a same-family pilot, a freeze through the canonical freezer and one confirmation produce committed receipts for the six cells of `adoption-family`.
- [hard] REQ-03: When the canonical evaluator reports `qualifies` true, each component the candidate carries lands. A variant replaces the check row with the contract suites passing and no second form or runtime selector. A QC route is selected by the committed envelope that production and the tuned arm install.
- [hard] REQ-04: Otherwise production's check row and default route stay unchanged, and the receipts are preserved as a negative or inconclusive result. A delivered QC route stays unselected, and the outcome names it.
- [hard] REQ-05: Adopted behavior stays within `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md`.

planning.outcome: Candidate confirmed against pre-change production; adopted only if it qualifies

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One existing family flow on six cells, with at most a one-function landing and an envelope change

title: Close the integrated LDPC cells against AFF3CT
description:
Close the epic with a recorded result for each of the four losing cells, and report the two one-worker eight-frame cells, against AFF3CT's matched decoder [Cassagne2019].

## Background

The losing cells are DVB-T2 R1/2 and NR BG1 Z=384 at `w1-b1` and `p12-b8`; the reported cells are the same codes at `w1-b8`. Earlier values are in `dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/1358d6ab/outcome.md`. The family is fixed by the contract `comparator-family` in `dev/active/55c3e433-aff3ct-ldpc-gaps/plan.md`. Timed runs execute only in the overnight benchmark window, and arming a window needs the owner's approval.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: When the epic adopted a production change, a same-family pilot, a freeze and one confirmation produce committed receipts for `comparator-family`. When it adopted none, no new campaign runs and the record says so.
- [hard] REQ-02: A generated outcome table gives each losing cell exactly one of a confirmed result against AFF3CT, a measured limit, or a preserved negative or inconclusive experiment, citing the committed artifact. Timing rows state the interval and sample count, and quality rows state frame-error counts and Wilson intervals.
- [hard] REQ-03: The same table reports both `w1-b8` cells against the same comparator, stating whether the lead is preserved. Negative outcomes appear as recorded.
- [hard] REQ-04: The outcome states the direction of each ratio and evaluator label, and whether each losing cell meets or exceeds AFF3CT.
- [hard] REQ-05: The outcome records that no quantized, layered, reassociated or AFF3CT-sign variant entered production, and a go decision on QC-aware decoding is closed by its confirmation result.

planning.outcome: Each losing cell has a recorded terminal result; eight-frame cells are reported

terminal.worker_sized_reason: At most one existing family flow, projected through the shared campaign tables
